title: Your worship did not end with the last song.
paragraphs: Your worship did not end with the last song.

Romans 12:1 does not call you to raise only your hands.
It calls you to lay down your life.

Because it is easy to look holy for an hour.
Harder to be holy when nobody claps.
When the office is toxic.
When the bills are loud.
When your flesh wants comfort more than Christ.

Paul says, “present your bodies as a living sacrifice.”
Living.

Meaning this sacrifice keeps crawling off the altar.
Again and again.
Temptation. Pride. Compromise. Anger. Secret habits. Quiet rebellion.

God is not asking for performance.
He is asking for surrender.

Real faith is not confined to a church chair, a worship set, or a Sunday selfie.
Real faith shows up in your mouth when you are offended.
In your eyes when lust comes knocking.
In your schedule when prayer feels inconvenient.
In your choices when nobody would ever know.

This is worship.
Not hype.
Not image.
A life handed over to Jesus.

And the reason we can live surrendered is this: Christ first gave Himself for us.
We do not climb onto the altar to earn grace.
We come because grace found us there.
Jesus took the punishment for our sin, rose in power, and now calls us to belong fully to Him.

So today, do not just attend worship.
Become it.

Lay your attitude down.
Lay your appetites down.
Lay your plans down.
And let Jesus be Lord outside of Sunday.
